ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a common-emitter transistor amplifier circuit. The emitter is directly grounded; the collector is connected to +V_CC through resistor R_C; the base is connected to +V_CC through resistor R_B; the input terminal and output terminal respectively pass through coupling capacitors C1, C2, therefore in static DC analysis C1, C2 can be regarded as open circuits and ignored. Reasoning: Because the emitter is grounded, static U_CE is equal to the collector-to-ground voltage. It is required that U_CE=6 V, while V_CC=12 V, therefore the voltage drop on R_C is 12 V - 6 V = 6 V. It is known that R_C=3 kΩ, so the collector current I_C = 6 V / 3 kΩ = 2 mA. The transistor β=50, therefore the base current I_B = I_C/β = 2 mA / 50 = 40 μA. Since U_BE can be ignored, and R_B is connected from +12 V to the base, the voltage on R_B is approximately 12 V, so R_B = 12 V / 40 μA = 300 kΩ.

method.method_draft: From the image, ignore C1 and C2 for quiescent DC analysis. Since the emitter is grounded, UCE equals the collector voltage. To make UCE = 6 V with VCC = 12 V, the drop across RC is 12 - 6 = 6 V, so IC = 6 V / 3 kΩ = 2 mA. Then IB = IC/β = 2 mA/50 = 40 μA. Since UBE is negligible and RB is from +12 V to the base, RB = 12 V / 40 μA = 300 kΩ.
